content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato with the peel removed is a tuber that has been baked whole and then stripped of its skin. The flesh retains most of the nutrients, while the absence of the peel makes it softer and easier to eat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato is one of the world’s most consumed foods, with annual production exceeding 350 million tonnes.
Baking preserves more vitamin C than prolonged boiling, where the vitamin is lost in the water.
The potato skin holds most of the fiber and polyphenols, so removing it reduces these beneficial compounds.
Baked potatoes are a staple in many cuisines: in Russia as a side dish, in the US as a classic “baked potato” with toppings.
There are over 4,000 potato varieties, differing in flesh colour, taste and starch content.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Baked potato provides slow‑release energy, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium promotes normal heart function and helps regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Even without the skin, the flesh still contains a modest amount of fiber beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Baked potato is virtually fat‑free, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: If a potato has sprouted or shows green spots, it may contain toxic solanine and should be discarded.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Baked potato has a high GI, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potato.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Prolonged high‑temperature baking can create acrylamide, a potential carcinogen; avoid over‑browning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Baked potato without peel can be eaten plain, added to salads, soups, casseroles, or mashed. It pairs well with low‑fat cottage cheese, yogurt, herbs, and a drizzle of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked baked potatoes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in the oven or microwave to retain texture.
